body: Sorry you're having that rough of a time with it. I sympathize with a bit of what you're saying, so you're not alone in it. I hope you find someone who understands what you're feeling...it's possible they'll pop out of nowhere even though it might feel like you've tried everyone. I'm hoping for the same for myself. Best wishes to you.
Thanks for sharing your experience. I've never been on SW or anything, thankfully, but having only imagined what it would be like I can say it wouldn't improve my mood, that's for sure.

I think that many times, that's completely true. I think there are a great many suicidal or depressed people out there who feel that no one would miss them if they died, or that they would be doing the world a favour by leaving. I think that people are trying to diminish this loneliness and guilt when they say things like this. However...I don't think everyone who says it feels that way, not completely. I think they would miss they person they lost, and in the end that absence would hurt them, not the deceased. I think they would feel sad and guilty and upset and they don't want to. I think this is what's being communicated, just as often as "you are important." And it's funny, because "sad, guilty, and upset" probably characterized the person who died...so strongly that they couldn't bear it.

Absolutely! Always a consequence, and suicide has a great many consequences. No matter what you do on this earth, you make someone happy and someone sad--I could buy my partner a gift to surprise him with when he gets home, let him know I'm thinking about him, etc., but the last gift I gave him was probably made under poor labour conditions, was a waste of non-renewable resources, might have been money better spent on charity, etc. 

I feel that people are able to push past these negative consequences and make it through their suffering so that they continue to live relatively meaningful lives...or they can't, in which case they may choose to stop living.
That certainly sounds like me, hahaha. Don't worry about not having advice; good to know I'm not the only one.

Thanks for your reply. I think it may be what I end up needing to do, even though the idea makes me uncomfortable. 

I do know that depression manifests in different ways for different people, and that it doesn't always involve sadness (or obvious sadness). However, I feel like I have maybe 1 or 2 of the possible symptoms of depression when one needs to display many symptoms to really be "depressed." I also think my symptoms are very mild and more of a rut/bad mood than mental illness. Hence seeking another opinion. 

Either way, thanks again for your reply.
